decision_question: Which portfolio of identity, wallet, Discord, and Telegram authentication/linking components best fits identity-api as a platform- and chain-agnostic canonical identity service?

method.type: Saaty AHP with absolute option ratings

rating_scale.meaning: Direct fit, robust, and unusually strong for this system.
Useful in some contexts; meaningful limitations.
Substantial mismatch, immaturity, or operating burden.
Actively conflicts with the target or adds unacceptable risk.

criteria.name: Near-term channel fit
criteria.definition: Direct contribution to wallet connect/auth plus Discord and Telegram linking in the next implementation cycle.

criteria.name: identity-api architecture fit
criteria.definition: Preserves identity-api as canonical identity source of record and issuer, with credentials entering through adapters.

criteria.name: Chain/platform agnosticism
criteria.definition: Works across wallet namespaces, chains, browsers, native apps, bots, and non-wallet identities without distorting the core model.

criteria.name: User friction reduction
criteria.definition: Reduces connector prompts, redirects, repeat sign-ins, recovery friction, and cross-device effort.

criteria.name: Security/linking assurance
criteria.definition: Strength of proof, replay resistance, session binding, collision policy, phishing resistance, and account-takeover defenses.

criteria.name: Maturity/interoperability
criteria.definition: Standards status, provider support, operational precedent, library quality, and portability between implementations.

criteria.name: Time to production
criteria.definition: How quickly the option can be safely shipped with the current stack and team.

criteria.name: Sovereignty/exit
criteria.definition: Control of canonical data and keys, self-hosting, auditable source, replaceability, and vendor exit.

criteria.name: Session/SSO continuity
criteria.definition: Ability to resume without repeated wallet/social prompts across reloads, apps, and devices.

criteria.name: Operational burden/TCO
criteria.definition: Combined reliability, operational complexity, recurring commercial cost, and incident blast radius.

options.applicability: The canonical credential-link ledger, link-intent state machine, collision policy, session resume, and audience-specific token issuance belong here.
options.tradeoff: Highest build burden, but every other option becomes replaceable and composable instead of becoming a second source of truth.

options.applicability: Official OIDC authorization-code adapter gives Telegram parity with Discord while preserving provider-neutral subjects and proof records.
options.tradeoff: Newer ecosystem path; implementation must validate discovery/JWKS, issuer, audience, expiry, nonce/state, and PKCE.

options.applicability: Direct near-term credential adapter keyed by immutable Discord issuer + subject; use identify-only scope first.
options.tradeoff: OAuth linking must be bound to the initiating identity-api session and provider/client context; no username or email merging.

options.applicability: Best chat-native bridge for linking a bot interaction to an authenticated web identity or starting a link from Discord/Telegram.
options.tradeoff: Cross-device links are phishing/session-fixation targets; codes must be unique, short-lived, single-use, context-bound, and visibly confirmed.

options.applicability: Best returning-user login and recovery credential once wallet, Discord, or Telegram has established the canonical user.
options.tradeoff: Requires RP-ID/origin planning and recovery policy; synced passkeys optimize availability while device-bound authenticators offer stronger isolation.

options.applicability: Lowest-friction way to establish Telegram identity inside a Mini App and then link or resume the canonical identity-api user.
options.tradeoff: Only valid in the Telegram-hosted surface; requires strict server validation, freshness bounds, replay controls, and explicit linkage policy.

options.recommendation: BEST buy candidate if activation speed dominates
options.applicability: Broadest managed coverage of Discord, Telegram, passkeys, external wallets, SIWE/SIWS, and embedded wallets in one product.
options.tradeoff: Strongest shortcut also creates the strongest risk of an external common-user object becoming the real identity authority.

options.recommendation: TRANSITION benchmark — do not deepen SoR dependency
options.applicability: Fast multi-wallet/social onboarding and existing ecosystem precedent; useful as a migration source or temporary credential provider.
options.tradeoff: Conflicts with the ratified identity-api SoR direction if its user/session model remains canonical.

options.applicability: Pragmatic way to reduce wallet connector approvals while keeping identity-api as nonce, verifier, user, and session authority.
options.tradeoff: One-Click Auth coverage is capability- and wallet-dependent; the practical implementation is strongest on EVM, so legacy and non-EVM fallbacks remain necessary.

options.applicability: Useful implementation substrate for OIDC/social/passkey UX behind identity-api's CredentialBridge and proof-normalization contract.
options.tradeoff: Its native user/account/session model must not silently become the canonical identity plane already owned by identity-api.

options.applicability: Broad chain support, Discord OAuth, external wallets, and custom JWT/OIDC make it compatible with identity-api as upstream identity.
options.tradeoff: Telegram still needs a separate adapter and the threshold-key network becomes another critical dependency.

options.applicability: Strong Telegram, SIWE, OTP/social, device binding, and auth-method linking for embedded-wallet products.
options.tradeoff: No comparable native Discord emphasis in the current product surface and a wallet-account model that can compete with identity-api.

options.applicability: Best fit for chain-neutral account identifiers and a provider-neutral signed-proof envelope inside identity-api.
options.tradeoff: The standards are not themselves a wallet transport or turnkey UX and remain less deployed than SIWE.

options.applicability: Fast social/passkey/Discord and embedded-wallet onboarding with strong transaction abstractions.
options.tradeoff: No first-class Telegram fit in the reviewed surface and a broad product footprint that can increase lock-in.

options.applicability: Architecturally closest chain-neutral answer to authenticating before an account has been separately exposed.
options.tradeoff: Excellent interface shape but insufficient broad wallet support for a production baseline.

options.applicability: Strongest managed security/policy option when identity-api needs downstream embedded wallets or agent wallets without outsourcing identity.
options.tradeoff: Does not solve Discord/Telegram linking by itself and introduces enclave, sub-organization, policy, and vendor operating models.

options.applicability: Mature standards broker if external enterprise IdPs, workforce federation, or policy administration become dominant requirements.
options.tradeoff: Adds another stateful identity runtime and still leaves wallet/chat-specific linking semantics to identity-api.

options.recommendation: PILOT only when repeated delegation is needed
options.applicability: Can authorize a device/account-specific identity key and scoped capabilities, reducing repeated wallet-key prompts for advanced flows.
options.tradeoff: Material protocol, key-lifecycle, revocation, and policy complexity before a concrete delegated-action use case exists.

options.applicability: Reliable fallback for wallets that lack combined authentication and for existing consumers already built around SIWE.
options.tradeoff: EVM-specific and usually retains separate connect and sign wallet approvals on first use.

options.recommendation: OPTIONAL EVM lane — not platform default
options.applicability: Excellent passkey-backed one-tap experience for supported EVM applications and payments.
options.tradeoff: Base/EVM-centered identity/account semantics conflict with identity-api's inherent cross-chain and non-wallet scope.

options.applicability: May be retained temporarily where migration cost is material.
options.tradeoff: Superseded by the official OIDC path and less aligned with a uniform OAuth/OIDC linking state machine.

options.applicability: Useful capability-detected EVM route to one combined connector interaction.
options.tradeoff: Draft, EVM-only, and overlaps with competing wallet-authentication interfaces.

options.applicability: Potential future zero-prompt reauthentication after a user grants an exact wallet-managed trust policy.
options.tradeoff: Review-stage proposal with no reliable wallet coverage and open product/security questions around policy management and auto-signing.

recommended_portfolio.owns: Canonical user_id; immutable provider issuer+subject keys; credential state; provenance; collision/revocation ledger.
recommended_portfolio.does_not_own: Provider profile content, wallet assets, Discord/Telegram community state.
recommended_portfolio.why: Makes every provider and wallet implementation replaceable while preserving one person across channels.
recommended_portfolio.acceptance: Unique(provider, issuer, subject); no username/email merge; collision is an explicit hard stop.
recommended_portfolio.kill: Kill or narrow if a second canonical user store is required to make it work.

recommended_portfolio.decision: Build once, reuse for Discord and Telegram
recommended_portfolio.owns: Initiating session, provider/toolkit/tenant/client context, state, nonce, PKCE challenge, redirect, expiry, one-time consumption.
recommended_portfolio.why: The 2026 OAuth threat model shows that PKCE alone does not prevent wrong-user or wrong-toolkit linkage.
recommended_portfolio.acceptance: The user who starts the link must be the user who completes it; exact provider context survives every redirect.
recommended_portfolio.kill: Reject designs that carry an unauthenticated raw user_id in a deep link or callback.

recommended_portfolio.owns: Discord code exchange, subject verification, normalized CredentialProof.
recommended_portfolio.why: High maturity, direct near-term need, and near-zero architectural conflict.
recommended_portfolio.acceptance: Authorization code + PKCE where applicable; exact redirect; immutable Discord subject; identify-only scope first.
recommended_portfolio.kill: Do not auto-link by Discord username, display name, or email.

recommended_portfolio.owns: OIDC discovery/JWKS, code exchange, ID-token validation, normalized CredentialProof.
recommended_portfolio.why: Official OIDC now provides a cleaner, standards-aligned path than the legacy widget.
recommended_portfolio.acceptance: S256 PKCE; validate issuer, audience, expiry, nonce/state; key by issuer+sub.
recommended_portfolio.kill: Do not start new legacy-widget integrations unless a documented platform constraint requires it.

recommended_portfolio.owns: Short-lived one-time code, context binding, bot identity proof, confirmation/audit event.
recommended_portfolio.does_not_own: Persistent identity authority in the bot.
recommended_portfolio.why: Most natural entry point for Discord/Telegram communities and support flows.
recommended_portfolio.acceptance: Unique code; very short TTL; single use; same-user binding; visible account being linked; rate limits.
recommended_portfolio.kill: Do not treat a forwarded deep link or bot message alone as sufficient identity proof.

recommended_portfolio.owns: Opaque server session, device/session metadata, refresh/resume, logout, revocation, audience-specific access tokens.
recommended_portfolio.does_not_own: Wallet connector state as authentication truth.
recommended_portfolio.why: This is what makes returning authentication genuinely zero-wallet-prompt.
recommended_portfolio.acceptance: Reload/redeploy does not force wallet or social reauthentication inside policy lifetime.
recommended_portfolio.kill: Do not persist bearer tokens or authenticated booleans as the primary browser source of truth.

recommended_portfolio.owns: Nonce, client/domain/audience, chain request, expiry, exact completion checks.
recommended_portfolio.why: Combined wallet authentication cannot work if the server requires an address before issuing the challenge.
recommended_portfolio.acceptance: Intent can be created before account exposure; recovered/verified account is bound only at completion.
recommended_portfolio.kill: Reject any one-click design that trusts a client-supplied address without proof.

recommended_portfolio.does_not_own: Nonce, proof validation, canonical user, or session.
recommended_portfolio.why: Best practical connector-level friction reducer available now.
recommended_portfolio.acceptance: One combined wallet request where supported; safe automatic fallback elsewhere.
recommended_portfolio.kill: Do not make Reown's account/session model the canonical identity record.

recommended_portfolio.why: Maximizes current wallet compatibility while one-click standards mature.
recommended_portfolio.acceptance: Domain/URI/nonce/chain/time checks; EIP-1271/6492 as needed; clear two-step fallback UX.
recommended_portfolio.kill: Do not represent it as chain-neutral.

recommended_portfolio.component: CAIP account IDs and proof envelope
recommended_portfolio.owns: Chain-neutral identifiers and normalized wallet proof vocabulary.
recommended_portfolio.why: Prevents an EVM-first route from shaping the canonical identity schema.
recommended_portfolio.acceptance: CAIP-2 chain ID + CAIP-10 account ID; proof_type/version; raw evidence reference; verifier metadata.
recommended_portfolio.kill: Avoid overbuilding CACAO capability semantics until a consumer requires them.

recommended_portfolio.owns: initData validation, freshness, replay and link/resume decision.
recommended_portfolio.acceptance: Server-verifiable HMAC/signature, max age, one-time link intent, explicit collision handling.
recommended_portfolio.kill: Do not accept unvalidated client-decoded initData.

recommended_portfolio.owns: WebAuthn credential records, authentication ceremony, recovery policy.
recommended_portfolio.why: Best returning-user credential and a wallet-independent recovery path.
recommended_portfolio.acceptance: RP/origin design; user-verification policy; multiple authenticators; revocation/recovery; AAL policy.
recommended_portfolio.kill: Do not promise AAL3 with synced passkeys.

recommended_portfolio.owns: Provider-specific OAuth/passkey UX and ceremony helpers behind a narrow port.
recommended_portfolio.does_not_own: Canonical user, link policy, issuer, or final session contract.
recommended_portfolio.why: Can accelerate social/passkey work without reversing the ratified architecture.
recommended_portfolio.acceptance: Every Better Auth result is translated into identity-api CredentialProof before standing is granted.
recommended_portfolio.kill: Stop if two-way user/session synchronization becomes required.

recommended_portfolio.owns: Embedded key infrastructure and app-facing wallet UX only.
recommended_portfolio.why: Useful only when a world explicitly needs embedded wallets, gas sponsorship, agent wallets, or key policies.
recommended_portfolio.acceptance: BYO-auth or external-user mapping, export/exit test, incident boundary, cost and SLA review.
recommended_portfolio.kill: Do not select a vendor merely to avoid implementing Discord/Telegram linking.

recommended_portfolio.why: Potentially valuable for repeated agentic or wallet actions after the simpler system is measured.
recommended_portfolio.acceptance: Explicit capability, expiry, revocation, device binding, and a named consumer.
recommended_portfolio.kill: Do not build without a measured repeated-signature problem.

sources.title: Log In With Telegram — OIDC
sources.claim: OIDC authorization-code flow, discovery/JWKS, and PKCE support for Telegram login.

sources.title: Legacy Telegram Login Widget
sources.claim: Legacy signed-widget option retained only for migration comparison.

sources.title: Telegram Mini Apps
sources.claim: Mini App initData is a chat-native authenticated context that must be validated server-side.

sources.title: OAuth2 and Permissions
sources.claim: Authorization-code OAuth is the standard Discord identity proof and linking transport.

sources.title: Discord Account Linking
sources.claim: Discord supports explicit application account-linking patterns.

sources.title: Account Linking on Mobile
sources.claim: PKCE and redirect binding are especially important for native/mobile account-linking flows.

sources.title: RFC 9700 — OAuth 2.0 Security Best Current Practice
sources.claim: Use authorization code, PKCE S256, exact redirects, issuer/context checks, and transaction binding.

sources.title: Updates to OAuth 2.0 Security BCP
sources.claim: COAT and cross-user session fixation require provider/toolkit/tenant isolation and same-user start/finish binding; PKCE alone is insufficient.

sources.title: Cross-Device Flows: Security Best Current Practice
sources.claim: Deep-link and QR flows need unique, short-lived, single-use codes, request binding, confirmation, and abuse controls.

sources.title: CAIP-122 — Sign-In With X
sources.claim: Provider-neutral sign-in message model using chain/account identifiers beyond Ethereum.

sources.title: CAIP-196 — CACAO
sources.claim: Common proof/capability envelope for SIWx, SIWE, UCAN, and multiple signature types.

sources.title: CAIP-222 — wallet_authenticate
sources.claim: Bundles account exposure and cryptographic authentication in one request before the account is known.

sources.title: EIP-4361 — Sign-In with Ethereum
sources.claim: Canonical EVM wallet-auth message with nonce, origin, chain, time, and resource binding.

sources.title: AppKit One-Click Auth
sources.claim: Preferred practical path to combine WalletConnect session establishment and SIWE authentication when supported.

sources.title: AppKit SIWX
sources.claim: CAIP-122-oriented multi-chain wallet authentication and capability detection.

sources.title: ERC-7846 — wallet_connect
sources.claim: Provider-level proposal to combine wallet connection and SIWE into one wallet interaction.

sources.title: ERC-8019 — Wallet-Managed Auto-Login for SIWE
sources.claim: Future wallet-local allowlist for zero-prompt SIWE after explicit trust policy.

sources.title: Identity Keys
sources.claim: A wallet can authorize a device/account-specific identity key to reduce repeated blockchain-key signatures.

sources.title: Wallet Authentication and ReCaps
sources.claim: Authenticated wallet sessions can carry scoped capabilities through ReCaps.

sources.title: Generic OAuth
sources.claim: Generic OAuth/OIDC adapters and explicit link-account endpoint requiring an existing session.

sources.title: Passkey Plugin
sources.claim: WebAuthn/FIDO2 passkey enrollment and sign-in, including conditional UI.

sources.title: Keycloak Documentation 26.7
sources.claim: Self-hosted OIDC/OAuth identity brokering, administration, and authorization services.

sources.title: Ory Documentation
sources.claim: Modern authentication, user management, and OAuth/OIDC building blocks with multiple deployment models.

sources.title: Web Authentication Level 3
sources.claim: Origin/RP-scoped public-key credentials with user verification and phishing-resistant authentication.

sources.title: SP 800-63B-4 — Syncable Authenticators
sources.claim: Synced passkeys can support AAL2 with controls but do not satisfy the non-exportability expected at AAL3.

sources.title: Device-Bound vs. Synced Credentials
sources.claim: Synced passkeys improve availability and recovery but concentrate security in the passkey provider; device-bound credentials offer stronger isolation.

sources.title: Privy Authentication
sources.claim: Common user object spanning Discord, Telegram, passkeys, OAuth, email/SMS, and SIWE/SIWS wallet login.

sources.title: Privy Embedded Wallets
sources.claim: Broad multi-chain embedded-wallet infrastructure, policy controls, and key export paths.

sources.title: Dynamic Headless Wallet Management
sources.claim: External/embedded wallet discovery, multi-wallet linking, social auth, and custom UI support.

sources.title: Dynamic Security Overview
sources.claim: Managed auth and wallet security architecture using layered controls and secure wallet infrastructure.

sources.title: Wallet Authentication
sources.claim: Email/SMS/social authentication including Telegram, plus embedded user wallets.

sources.title: Auth Method Linking
sources.claim: Explicit linking of OAuth, OTP, and SIWE methods to a signed-in user.

sources.title: Embedded Wallets Authentication
sources.claim: External wallets, Discord and other OAuth providers, plus custom JWT/OIDC identity integration.

sources.title: Embedded Wallets Architecture
sources.claim: Threshold key-share architecture that can sit downstream of an existing JWT identity layer.

sources.title: Embedded Wallets Overview
sources.claim: Passkey/social/OTP auth, multi-chain wallets, enclave key management, policies, and custody choices.

sources.title: Wallets
sources.claim: Rapid embedded wallet onboarding using social, passkey, external-wallet, and account-abstraction flows.

sources.title: Base Account Overview
sources.claim: Passkey-backed universal sign-on and smart-wallet identity across supported EVM networks.

caveats: Ratings are analyst judgments anchored to primary documentation, not measured conversion, incident, or cost data.
Commercial pricing and contract terms change frequently and require vendor quotes.
Standards labeled Draft or Review should be capability-detected and kept behind stable internal interfaces.
The model ranks contribution to the target architecture; it does not imply that mutually complementary components are substitutes.
